lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality, personal details conventionally left off.
items.because: Readers should not weigh them as qualifications, and they use space without strengthening evidence of fit.

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first.
items.because: Crestline ended in 2023 but appears above the 2024 Harbor internship, making the section harder to scan chronologically.

items.says: Education appears before Experience and Projects.
items.because: Readers encounter degrees before the work and product direction they support.

items.says: The bullet presents a change in the on-time calculation as an actual reduction in late deliveries.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can lower the reported rate without changing how many deliveries were late.

items.says: The first-person pronoun “my” does not belong in a résumé bullet.
“Was rolled out with” obscures who implemented the redesign.
The forecast-error result does not name the error measure.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what “forecast error” measures or compare the result with other forecasting outcomes.

items.says: The forecast-error result is buried after the review description and scope.
“S&OP” may be unfamiliar to readers outside the team.
The route-planning rollout and its result should lead the Crestline entry.
items.because: Its clear initiative and quantified annual saving make it the most immediately legible impact.

items.says: The 35% conversion improvement has no baseline or comparison period.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the increase was measured against or how to interpret its size.

items.says: “For all merchants” is a broad qualifier that adds little to the result.
The bullet gives the delivery schedule but not the feature’s post-launch effect.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the feature mattered to users or the business after launch.

items.says: The shipping result comes late and refers vaguely to “it.”
The chargeback-loss estimate does not identify the merchant population it covers.
The roadmap impact appears only after the methods and estimate.
“The business case that set the next quarter’s roadmap priority” is wordy.
“Over the summer” repeats timing already supplied by the role dates.
The comparison method is given without its outcome or result.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what outcome was measured or whether the redesign improved onboarding.

items.says: The 9-to-4-day onboarding result is attributed to both the Harbor internship and the hospital-network practicum.
items.because: The practicum predates the internship, and its hospital context does not fit the merchant-payment claim.

items.says: “Around a single verification step” describes the redesign indirectly.
items.because: Stating the step plainly would make the process change quicker to understand.

items.says: The line does not say how the app enabled food pickups.
items.because: A concrete feature or workflow would clarify the product contribution behind the result.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” is wordy and hypothetical.
“After 60 user interviews showed” makes the interviews sound like the direct trigger for the reminders.
The scheduling sessions are described without a resulting change.
items.because: Without a concrete scheduling outcome, the value of the practicum is difficult to judge.

items.says: The intake change is described without saying what it improved.
items.because: Staff adoption does not show whether intake became faster, simpler or less error-prone.

items.says: The intake bullet should open the practicum entry.
items.because: Its concrete work across four clinics and staff adoption provide the clearest evidence of the practicum’s work.

items.says: Passive constructions hide who mapped intake and shortened the form.
The merchant-onboarding achievement does not fit the hospital-network practicum.
items.because: The other practicum bullets concern clinics, while the merchant-payment outcome is also attributed to Harbor.

items.says: “By redesigning onboarding” does not specify what changed in the process.
items.because: The claimed outcome is not connected to a concrete intervention.

items.says: “It takes” uses present tense for a completed result.
items.because: The inconsistent timing can interrupt a reader’s understanding of the result.

items.says: “Across 2,300 merchants” interrupts the phrase describing the time reduction.
items.because: Separating the time measure from its result makes the claim harder to scan.
